title: Inverse image along composable open immersions agrees with iterated restriction
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $k:V\hookrightarrow U$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]; put $l=j\circ k$. For an open immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow Y$ and $G\in\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ let $\rho_aG$ be the restriction of $G$, $(\rho_aG)(T\xrightarrow{\varphi}W)=G(T\xrightarrow{a\varphi}Y)$ with the same restriction maps, and let $\theta_{a,G}:a^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_aG$ be the natural identification of the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] with the restriction given in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Then $\rho_k\rho_jG=\rho_lG$ as sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $V_{\Et}$, and the module-linear composition isomorphism $c_{j,k,G}:k^{-1}j^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}l^{-1}G$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] satisfies $$\theta_{l,G}\circ c_{j,k,G}=\rho_k(\theta_{j,G})\circ\theta_{k,j^{-1}G}:k^{-1}j^{-1}G\to \rho_k\rho_jG=\rho_lG,$$ naturally in $G$.

source.place: Tag 03EH (lemma-relocalize): $j_V^{-1}=j^{-1}\circ j_U^{-1}$ for successive localizations; with etale-cohomology.tex after Definition 03S3 (definition-extension-zero): $j^{-1}$ is restriction along $U_{\Et}\to X_{\Et}$

proof.text: For every object $T\xrightarrow{\varphi}V$ of the small etale site, the defining formula gives $(\rho_k\rho_jG)(T\xrightarrow{\varphi}V)=G(T\xrightarrow{\varphi}V\xrightarrow{k}U\xrightarrow{j}X)=G(T\xrightarrow{l\varphi}X)=(\rho_lG)(T\xrightarrow{\varphi}V)$. The restriction maps for both sides are the restriction maps of $G$ along the same composites, so these equalities identify $\rho_k\rho_jG$ and $\rho_lG$ strictly as sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03EH (lemma-relocalize), together with the explicit restriction description after Definition 03S3 in etale-cohomology.tex

proof.text: For an open immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow Y$ put $S_W=S\times_YW$ for $S\in Y_{\Et}$. The direct-image definition gives $(a_*F)(S)=F(S_W)$. The adjunction $\rho_a\dashv a_*$ can be checked directly: a map $\alpha:\rho_aG\to F$ gives $\beta_S:G(S)\to F(S_W)$ by $s\mapsto\alpha_{S_W}(s|_{S_W})$. Conversely, for $T\in W_{\Et}$, set $\alpha_T=\beta_T$ after the canonical identification $T\times_YW\cong T$, since $a$ is an open immersion. These assignments are inverse: on $T$ the projection $T\times_YW\to T$ is an isomorphism, and on $S$ their composite is $\beta_S$ by naturality for $S_W\to S$. They commute with module scalars and sheaf maps. Taking $F=\rho_aG$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ shows that the unit in this restriction model sends $s\in G(S)$ to $s|_{S_W}$.

source.place: After Definition 03S3 (definition-extension-zero), restriction description; explicit adjunction calculation using the direct-image definition

proof.text: The cited extension-by-zero adjunction statement identifies $a^{-1}G(T\to W)$ with $G(T\to Y)$, giving exactly $\theta_{a,G}$. Its compatibility with the unit of $a^{-1}\dashv a_*$ is also explicit from the definition of inverse image: the presheaf inverse-image generator represented by $s\in G(S)$ and $T\to S$ over $Y$ maps to $s|_T\in G(T)$. This respects the restriction relations and hence the sheafification defining $a^{-1}G$. Applied to the unit on $S$, with $T=S_W$ and its projection to $S$, it gives $\theta_{a,G}(\eta_{a,G,S}(s))=s|_{S_W}$, with $a_*$ understood on $\theta$. Thus $\theta$ identifies the inverse-image unit with the restriction-model unit computed in Step 2. This applies to $j,k,l$, naturally in $G$.

source.place: After Definition 03S3 (definition-extension-zero); inverse-image identification evaluated on presheaf generators

proof.text: Set $r_G=\rho_k(\theta_{j,G})\circ\theta_{k,j^{-1}G}$ and $h_G=\theta_{l,G}^{-1}\circ r_G$. We check the unit equation characterizing $c_{j,k}$ in the two cited composition statements. For $S\in X_{\Et}$ write $S_U=S\times_XU$, $S_V=S\times_XV$. Under Step 3 the composite unit $j_*\eta_kj^{-1}\circ\eta_j$, followed by $j_*k_*(r_G)$, sends $s\in G(S)$ first to $s|_{S_U}$ and then to $(s|_{S_U})|_{S_U\times_UV}$. The right-hand side $d_{j,k,\rho_lG}\circ\eta_l$ in the restriction model sends it first to $s|_{S_V}$ and then restricts along the canonical isomorphism $S_U\times_UV\to S_V$, by clause (1) of the abelian composition statement. These are the same map: both restrict $s$ along the composite projection $S_U\times_UV\to S$. Naturality of $d$ with respect to $\theta_{l,G}$ and cancellation of its isomorphism therefore give $j_*k_*(h_G)\circ j_*\eta_kj^{-1}\circ\eta_j=d_{j,k,l^{-1}G}\circ\eta_l$. The maps $h_G$ are natural module isomorphisms, since they are composites of such maps. The uniqueness clause of the module-linear composition statement implies $h=c_{j,k}$. Multiplying by $\theta_l$ proves the required equality, with the endpoint equality of Step 1. No finiteness or torsion hypothesis on $\Lambda$ was used.

Sources checked: Stacks 03EH lemma-relocalize (sites.tex l.5455), 03S3 and the following text on restriction (etale-cohomology.tex l.11361-11420), and 03D8 (sites-modules.tex l.1236). The proof origin is correctly marked agent. The statement is well-typed. theta is canonical because (T, T≅T×_Y W) is initial in the presheaf-pullback index category. The coefficients are a general commutative Lambda with the constant sheaf, and the parent's finite Lambda is a special case. I tested id j and id k, V empty, G=0 and Lambda=0. I recomputed Steps 1-4 by hand. Step 1 is the strict equality from the definition. Step 2 gives the adjunction and the unit s↦s|_{S_W}. Step 3 shows theta carries the inverse-image unit to that unit through the generators (s, S_W→S). Step 4: both sides send s to s|_{S_U×_U V}; naturality of d at theta_l and cancellation give the clause (2) unit equation for h, so h=c by uniqueness. The module linearity of theta holds at presheaf level, and the abelian uniqueness gives h=c anyway. Each step uses only the cited statements, never their proofs. There are no new nodes.
